subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Self-Healing Concrete for Bridges
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Self-Healing Concrete for Bridges.

hook.text: Concrete cracks. It always has. But what if it could fix itself like skin healing a cut?

buildup.text: Researchers embed bacteria or capsules of healing agents in concrete. When cracks form, the agents activate.

discovery.text: Bacillus bacteria produce limestone when exposed to water and air through cracks. They literally fill the gap.

twist.text: The bacteria can survive dormant inside concrete for up to 200 years, waiting for a crack to appear.

climax.text: Self-healing concrete could save billions in bridge maintenance. The Netherlands is testing it on real structures.

punchline.text: Living concrete. It heals its own wounds.

quiz.question: How do bacteria help self-healing concrete repair cracks?
options: They eat away damaged material to reveal fresh layers
They produce limestone when exposed to water through cracks
They release gas that expands to fill gaps mechanically
